entry.title: The Human Touch: Why Human-Curated Radio Beats Spotify's AI Algorithms
entry.summary: Let me tell you about a specific experience that changed how I think about music discovery. It was a Tuesday night, sometime around midnight. I was building something, tired, probably should have stopped an hour earlier. A radio station I had on — Radio Paradise, human-curated — played a track I had never heard before. Something between post-rock and ambient electronic. I stopped what I was doing and just listened. That song became one of my most-played tracks of the year. Spotify's algorithm, despite knowing my listening history in granular detail, had never once surfaced it in the two years I had a premium account. A human DJ found it for me in 30 seconds. That's the thing about algorithms: they're very good at giving you more of what you already know you like. They're genuinely terrible…

So, I built gpushx — a lightweight, developer-friendly CLI that brings the entire workflow into the terminal. gpushx is a smart CLI tool that lets you: Create GitHub repositories Push branches Create Gists Merge PRs Deploy to Vercel (frontend) Deploy to Render (backend) …all with simple, memorable commands. Cron expressions are everywhere in development. entry.summary: Hello all we are VendlyPrivacyLabs. Privacy tools is something we believe everyone should have access to and not just access open source and free. Why? Because privacy is a right and these days it been made harder to maintain your privacy. So this is why we decided to launch a privacy suite with tools that most will find helpful. We didn't just stop there we thought why not also offer ease of use...so we also built some of our services to work through TWAs. So what are some of the tools you maybe asking? EXIF Stripper Secure Notes File Encryptor OTR Chat PDF Metadata Scrubber Why open source? Why free? Auditable code matters because trust shouldn't be blind. You shouldn't have to take our word for it that we're not logging your files or reading your notes. You should be able to look at the code yourself, or have someone you trust look at it. That's why everything we build is open source. Check it, fork it, self-host it if you want complete control. Privacy used to be the default. You had a conversation, it stayed between the people in the room. You sent a letter, only the recipient opened it. Somewhere along the way that flipped — now sharing everything is the default and privacy is something you have to actively fight for. We don't think that's acceptable, and we're not going to build tools that make it worse. This isn't a startup play. There's no exit strategy here, no plan to sell to an ad network, no investor pushing us toward monetisation. Just tools that work, code you can read, and the belief that privacy should be a standard — not a privilege. Vendlyprivacylabs.

entry.title: I wrote a PowerShell script to guess my PC's resale value (and learned my depreciation math was wrong)
entry.summary: Tried selling my old laptop last month. eBay sold listings were all over the place. Same model, same year, prices ranging from $180 to $420.
